_: mg-937c — THE DECLARED BASELINE, WHICH IS THE OWNERS LIST AND NOT A COUNT.
what_this_is: One row per VERDICT-STALE transcript in the record, both passes.  It is the
baseline `the list has not grown` is graded against AND it is the per-instance
ownership mg-30bd's README §8 item 1 left open, deliberately in ONE file: a
baseline that is not a list of things somebody read is a number that launders
whatever was true on the day it was taken, which is why mg-30bd refused to set
one.  You cannot declare this baseline without naming a cause for every entry.
NOTHING REGENERATES THIS FILE.  It is a hand-maintained declaration like
code/control_gate_724a/BASELINE.json, and `owners_937c.py` is what compares it
to the record.  So it is itself a member of the class this directory counts,
and the arm is the comparison that keeps it honest.
what_the_arm_can_and_cannot_check: CAN: that every stale entry in the record has a row (growth), that no row's
class has strengthened, that `read` matches whether the record quotes the whole
move, and that `cause: RECORD-DISAGREES` agrees with the record's own
disagreement.  Those four are falsifiable and three of them are hand fields.
CANNOT: that a cause is the RIGHT cause.  Nothing here can check a judgement
about why a verdict moved, and pretending otherwise is the laundering this file
exists to avoid.  `owner` is DERIVED FROM THE DIRECTORY NAME — it is an ADDRESS,
not a consent, and no agent has agreed to any row by its presence here.
what_declared_rows_is: THE SIZE OF THIS BASELINE ON THE DAY IT WAS DECLARED, and it is here because
mg-5491 needed it to be a MEASUREMENT rather than a sentence.  The list moves --
rows retire when somebody repairs a transcript, rows arrive when somebody
re-measures a suite -- so `150` became a figure this directory's prose stated
and none of its transcripts printed, which is exactly the class mg-2959's arm
counts.  The arm prints this beside the live count, so the two are read
together and the movement is visible instead of being an unexplained edit.
IT IS A HAND FIELD AND NOTHING CHECKS IT.  It is a claim about a commit that
has already happened (cd28bd2); the honest defence is that it is stated as a
date-stamped declaration and not as a live property.
how_to_move_a_value: A row LEAVES when its transcript is no longer VERDICT-STALE in the record — the
arm prints the exact deletion and stays GREEN, because going red when somebody
repairs a transcript is mg-e35b's red-on-improvement.
A row ARRIVES only with a cause and a disposition, from the vocabularies below,
assigned by reading the entry in out_verdict_staleness.txt.  A row added to
silence the arm without that reading is the defect, not the fix.
what_walk_lines_is: mg-cda7 — ONE ENTRY PER QUOTED LINE INSIDE A `HISTORY-WALK` ROW, with a hand
verdict on whether that LINE is a row of a git-log walk.  It exists because the
in-family / out-of-family split mg-aff1 reports is a proxy over PATHS: a line
counts in-family because the ROW it sits in was read and filed HISTORY-WALK, not
because anybody looked at the line.  So a widening confined to these rows leaves
the OUT column at exactly where it was however wrong it is, and two of the
planted widenings in lib30bd.CANDIDATE_WIDENINGS do precisely that.
`owners_937c.py` §6b grades every candidate widening against this list, so
`OUT unmoved` stops being the whole defence and `gained N lines somebody read as
NOT-WALK` becomes a number a rule can fail on.  A widening that takes a NOT-WALK
line is a FINDING and exits 1: it is this directory's own file and the repair is
in the same commit — narrow the rule, or read the line again and say why.
CAN BE CHECKED: that every in-family quoted line in the record has an entry
(a new HISTORY-WALK row arrives UNREAD and is a finding), and that every entry
still occurs in the record (a stale entry is a finding).  Both directions, for
the reason `cause: RECORD-DISAGREES` is checked in both.
CANNOT: that a verdict is the RIGHT verdict.  Nothing checks a reading, which
is word for word what this file already declares about `cause`.  What stops it
being tuned to flatter the shipped rule is that §6b grades EVERY rule against
the same list and prints them side by side, including rules written after it.
KEYED BY DIGEST — 12 hex of sha256 over the stripped MASKED line, which is what
the record stores — because these lines run to 900 characters and a hand file is
unreadable at that width.  The excerpt beside it is what a reader reads; the
digest is what the arm matches on.

causes.LIVE-OUTSIDE-REPO: not a function of this repository at all — it reads state that lives outside the tree, so no commit can make it reproduce
causes.NONDETERMINISM: the producer is not deterministic on an unchanged tree
causes.DECLARED-UNREPRODUCIBLE: the transcript's own text says it must not be re-run, and the sweep re-ran it
causes.HISTORY-WALK: an unbounded history walk quoting commit subjects — moves when main moves (mg-e720's family)
causes.CORPUS-COUNT: a census figure over a growing corpus, sharing a line with a verdict token
causes.SUBJECT-MOVED: an audit of another ticket's artifact, and the artifact was changed after the audit was taken
causes.CONTROL-FLIPPED: this suite's own control or selftest reaches a different verdict on this tree
causes.RECORD-DISAGREES: the record contains a second graded observation of this transcript that does not agree, and the disagreeing one is not the owner's

dispositions.RE-MEASURE: this record cannot settle it — re-run the suite alone at a higher limit on a quiet host (§6.4, README §8 item 3)
dispositions.PIN-AS-DATED: the figure is a dated census; the repair is an as-of statement or a bounded population, not a new number
dispositions.BOUND-THE-WALK: mg-e720's repair — bound the walk, so the transcript stops being a function of how many commits main has
dispositions.UNTRACK-OR-PIN: the transcript is not a function of repo state; it cannot be a fixed point until it is made one or stops being tracked as evidence
dispositions.TICKET: a graded outcome genuinely moved and somebody has to decide which side is right.  This is the class that needs a work item per instance
